body:
My First Experience with 3.5g of Euphoria
1 Background
On March 28, 2018, at around 4pm, I consumed 3.5g of dried psilocybe cubensis. This proved to be an incredibly euphoric and spiritual journey, one that I will never forget.  To preface, I had spent about one week prior preparing and hyping for this trip. I had thought of all this stuff to watch, music to listen to, songs to play on guitar. I was prepared. As you will soon gather, I was not the driver of this trip; I was but an impotent passenger. Thus, the majority of these specific aspirations fell through. But did I really know what I was looking for?
After a restless night and stressful day, a speech and a presentation (HS senior), I finally make it back home. I am alone for the night and stoked out of my mind. I force down some food, despite my stomach resisting because of the pre-flight anxiety. I took the ziploc bag of mushrooms out of my backpack. They really are beautiful. I put them on a cutting board (no grinder), cut them up real small, dumped the powdery chunks in a cup, and poured a little shot of lemon juice in. After twenty minutes of nervously pacing around waiting for the psilocybin to convert form, I took the abhorrent mixture to my living room and brought orange juice as a chaser. The tan frothy mixture taunts me, waiting for me to act. I raise the glass to my lips, held it in my mouth for a split second, and before thinking, swallow.
Nasty! The only worse taste Ive known is that god awful DXM syrup. A few swings of the froth, many more of the orange juice, and I swish around the liquid for a final swig and then fiend away the dust remaining. The last gulp brought out a gag reflex, and I narrowly avoid vomit after swallowing quickly. I spend a few minutes exercising deep breaths trying not to throw up. Thank heavens I didnt.
2 Come Up
As I had previously planned, I walk into the woods to begin my trip. Not far in, I sense a rise in energy. Deep in me, it feels like there is a volcano rumbling, an ominous signal, preparing to release fire. I walk around a bit but quickly conclude it is simply unsafe to be this far from home and protection. Through the half melted rolling mounds of snow that decorate the forest, I trudge out of the woods and onto the dirt road. The road I walk on is beginning to, not exactly spin, I wouldnt say it is trembling, but something about it is tripping me the fuck out. I notice how detailed the road is, laden with gravel, rocks, dirt, and potholes. I walk past one of the neighborhood kids.
Hey N!
Hey!
As I approach my house, an internal debate erupts over whether I should check the mailbox at the end of the street. I end up taking up the challenge; though the side of my mind that wanted to go straight home is salty, and I cuss and shake my head at myself. I try to walk normal, but Im not sure what to do with my arms. When I at last reach the mailboxes, I let out a sigh of relief.
I start heading back from the mailbox, relieved by the notion of being safe at home once again. I glance around. Seeing no cars on the road and no humans outside, I start running, skipping, zigzagging across the street. My body is light. I approached my front lawn and the whole scene has this weed-like feel of an alien planet. I wouldnt quite describe my perception as blurry, because my vision is still clear, but it almost seems like everything is in 2D layers. When I move forward just a step it is as if there is too much depth change between the tree branches in front of my house and the towering pines way behind lining the horizon.
I get back inside my house. Being indoors now feels so small and claustrophobic, especially considering at this point the volcano inside me really wants to explode. The body load overwhelms me. This combined with classic come up anxiety prompt me to try to contact as many people as possible. I am not panicking just yet, but I am getting pretty hasty and irrational. My sister is on a bus, she cant talk. I tell her to call me as soon as she can, but I also say everythings fine so she wont worry. Everything is very urgent. Finally I find a friend whos online. V and I video chat via snapchat. Hes wearing earbuds sitting in a library working on a group project. He tries to be cordial, but my hyperstimulated mind only notes the slight lip raises and brief sounds of laughter that escape him.
He was laughing at me; it soon becomes a problem. His big ass grinning face and nose are seemingly larger than my tiny phone screen. Our conversation is pretty one sided; it mainly consists of me incoherently pouring out my every problem. I shouldnt have done this alone, why are you laughing at me, where is the TV remote... all in a sort of desperate, pleading manner. After what seems like quite a hefty battle, I was out of breath, half-yelling, pleading at the TV and V, I make it to the finish: pre-recorded episodes of Planet Earth II. The episode: mountains. I often hear Bob Ross and Planet Earth are the best medicines for bad trips. I part ways with V. Though my chat with him was panicked and he was laughing and I was a mess, (he was trying not to laugh, which I also noticed, but still) it kept me distracted, and thus was significantly better than if I spent that time on my own.
3 Beauty
I bring a bunch of blankets and pillows downstairs and spread them out on the living room floor. Wrapped in comforters, head peeping out, breathing slowly, I give my undivided attention to Sir Davids program. It is the safest possible thing I can be doing right now.  Planet Earth is fucking amazing. It takes place on some desert plateau in Ethiopia and Im watching these mountain gazelles scurry around on these nauseatingly high cliffs. Everything is augmented to have this blurry zigzag pattern and every sound, every footstep, every time a little deer hoof clicks onto the rocky ground, is magnified. Every detail is observed. The show shifts focus to the predator.
Behind the haze brought by the heat rising off of the earth, enter the predator. Its beady eyes pop out of the TV screen. The red wolf lands each hoof a step closer to me with such purpose. I am in awe of the natural beauty. When I'm under the influence of mushrooms I am closer to my animal/spirit and it makes watching Planet Earth much more profound. I watch the gazelles repeatedly outmaneuver the wolf. The dusty old caveman parts of my brain activate, picking up on animal communication and accept the natural hierarchies and flow of life and death.
My TV cuts to a commercial. My eyes hit the remote laying next to me, but the thought is immediately shot down. My arms crossed over my chest, my head pressing down against a pillow, my legs blanketed, it feels as though I am strapped into a capsule; there is not a chance I can will myself into raising my arm even an inch off the carpet.
So, tough shit, I cant fast forward through the commercials. The commercials provide a stark juxtaposition of the natural world and the super fast, loud, bright, artificial world. I specifically remember a Haribo gummy bear ad. The concept is already trippy: kids dressed in business attire discussing gummy flavors. Each kids head is ballooning out of their tux. The fast, high-pitched jingle sounds and I am blasted off into another commercial.
Planet Earth served great at calming me down, but eventually it loses my focus. I travel upstairs to the bathroom where I sit on the floor and try to decide what to do next. Decision making on psychs is clearly something to be avoided. It quickly becomes a thought loop debate and the dialogue in my head argues over laying in my bed with music versus going to the basement to play guitar versus watching more TV versus... eventually this begins to spiral out of control and I force quit the loop and head back to the cocoon of blankets facing the TV.
4 Rebirth
I unpause the Planet Earth, but just like last time, it seems to lose me. It serves as the backdrop of my thoughts instead of the engine. Shit gets weird. The words that follow can only give an extremely vague sense of what happened. I am still lying down in my capsule, eyes pointed at the TV. Though my eyes point at the TV, it seems that their function has become moot. Everything I see is in my head, sort of like if I close my eyes and try hard to imagine something. I have entered the psychedelic realm.
It is here where I meet T for the first time. I do not see him physically and do not hallucinate him, so I dont quite understand how he is with me, but he is. In those few important moments I understand his struggle. He seemingly welcomes me in with open arms as a parent does after their kids first day of kindergarten. I knew him before.
It is here where I meet T for the first time. I do not see him physically and do not hallucinate him, so I dont quite understand how he is with me, but he is. In those few important moments I understand his struggle. He seemingly welcomes me in with open arms as a parent does after their kids first day of kindergarten. I knew him before.
I realize our friendship has transcended the human realm. The love we share has existed since ancient times, throughout human civilizations and others. I have known his spirit in past lives, and more importantly, I will continue to be with his spirit in future lives. But our material lives dont matter as much, because where I am now is the central location of my spirit. I am finally home.
My tour through the psychedelic realm seems brief. When my focus comes back to the living room I have tears streaming down my cheekbones but neither from sadness nor euphoria. I am, however, very satisfied with what I have learned. I feel safe now. I feel a need to piss. You know, whenever Im sitting in physics and I feel a slight tingling the ol bladder I think, damn, how relieving would it be to simply release it all right here right now? I slither out of my cocoon of blankets. My back is on the floor and I am propelling myself across the carpet with my feet. Somewhere around this point my entire mindset becomes that of an infant. I slide my way over to the dining room.
Its time. My head sends the go-ahead signal to the appropriate muscles and I instantly feel sweet, warm piss running down my right thigh. Before too long I am laying in a puddle of urine that has soaked all around my pajamas, balls, and ass. Sweet sweet nasty relief. I kick down a chair. I get out of my pajamas, stand up, and take off my shirt. I glance around: in the kitchen a chair is toppled next to a miserable pool of piss and scrunched up soaking pajamas. In the living room, food trash on the couches and blankets and pillows scattered across the floor. I am VERY entertained by all of this destruction and chaos.
5 Rampage (Bing Bing!)
I am naked. I am an infant. I am an animal. I am chaos. I walk back to my blanketed area, the swively chair at the desk is in my way. BAM! I knock it on the ground. I see my plastic cup half full of water sitting on the desk. WHACK! Droplets fly everywhere and the cups slams the carpet. Me: 1 cup: 0. I start maniacally laughing. I am energized and euphoric. I start running around my house. I look at my hands as if they are foreign objects. Its as if I am in this body for the first time and everythings getting tested out. I am deeply humored by the mess I have created. I scream IVE BEEN A NAUGHTY BOY! multiple times. I start taking these massive alien steps, my feet stomping the floor each time while screaming BINGBING, BINGBING and BINGBINGBONGBONG, BINGBINGBONGBONG and WAPAPOWWEEEE *trailing into low pitched cartoon retarded person laughter. Slamming doors left and right, I sprint back and leap into the couch. I go to my iPod to blast Sacred Sands by the Allah-Las and let it play the rest of the album. I clamber up the stairs like a dog.
I step into the bathroom and immediately think water! I turn on the shower head and dance in the cold water like a child jumping around in a puddle. I dont stay in very long. I look at my middle finger. What happens if I do this? The dry finger rockets up my asshole. After sniffing the shit-infused finger, I shove it in my mouth and suck the disgusting inchoate matter right off. It tastes foul; I spit it out. I purposefully roll myself back down the stairs. I like to wonder how horrified someone at my door would be if they looked right into the kitchen as all of this was taking place. I probably couldve scarred a Jehovahs Witness into believing there is no God.
I am singing to No Voodoo with a deep, raspy, southern accent as loud as I can. I am vibing hard. I collapse on the floor many times. The final track contains the lyrics Its been a long, long journey, dont know where I left my mind. The music ends, and I finally decide to stop terrorizing my house and instead rest on the couch. What is without a doubt the most euphoric half an hour of my life comes to an end.
6 Come Down
Exhausted, I lay on my couch and look forward. The DVRd Planet Earth has long since ended, and the TV has returned to whatever cable channel I was previously watching. The current program is Law and Order, something I know of but never actually watch. Now normally a drama show would be ruined with a drug like weed because you begin to see through the acting, but the still very pronounced effect of the mushroom seems to do the opposite: I see so far through the acting that I see actual pain and emotion in the actors (instead of their characters.)
I pull out my phone and assure the appropriate people that everything is alright. It seems somewhere in my euphoric rampage I texted V  I WIN, I WIN and I just fucked Mrs. G get on my level you fucking walnut balloon. I also recorded myself stomping around screaming and remember being very close to posting it on my Snapchat story.
Anyways, I get a text from this drug degen kid who was trying to fiend some of the shrooms off me earlier that day. I wouldnt tell him where I got the stuff, so he angrily writes By the way, I know those shrooms are from A. Okay so is this some victory to you? I still have access to shrooms and you still dont amused, slightly annoyed, I wish him happy birthday. He asks if theres any way I can get him some and I leave him on read. I get pessimistic for a change. My house is trashed. How will I stop myself from hysterically laughing the second I walk into my French class tomorrow. Those academic tryhards havent seen SHIT. I am beginning to get a little anxious and depressed but I have a long, fruitful discussion via Snapchat with my friend A, and this gets my head out of the gutter. I suck it all up, clean up all my shit, make myself frozen pizza, and hit the bed. Its been a long day.
